# FreeToolHub

> 135+ free online tools for students, developers and professionals: PDF tools, image compression to an exact size in KB, finance and India-specific calculators, chemistry and math solvers. Everything runs in the browser with no signup.

FreeToolHub is a static website built in vanilla JavaScript. Tool processing happens locally on the visitor's device, and files are not uploaded to a server. Each tool has its own page at https://freetoolhub.app/tools/<name>.

## Guides

- [Photo or signature rejected on a government form? Check these 7 things](https://freetoolhub.app/blog/photo-signature-rejected-fixes): Why exam and government portals reject a photo or signature even when the size looks right: minimum size, format, dimensions, filename and more, with fixes.
- [UPSC photo and signature size: what the portal asks for](https://freetoolhub.app/blog/upsc-photo-signature-size): UPSC online application photo and signature file size and format, reported from the 2026 guidelines, with a link to the official instruction PDF and how to compress to fit.
- [SSC CGL signature size, and why there is no photo to upload](https://freetoolhub.app/blog/ssc-cgl-signature-size): SSC CGL 2026: the signature is a 10 to 20 KB JPG, while the photo is captured live. Reported specs, source links and how to compress your signature to fit.
- [Indian passport photo size: 4.5 x 3.5 cm, and when you need a photo at all](https://freetoolhub.app/blog/passport-photo-size-india): What the official Passport Seva instruction booklet says about the passport photo: size, background, face position, and why Seva Kendra applications need no photo.
- [How to calculate molar mass: worked examples from H2O to Al2(SO4)3](https://freetoolhub.app/blog/how-to-calculate-molar-mass): Step-by-step molar mass calculation with five worked examples, how to handle brackets, the mass percent of each element, and converting grams to moles.
- [How to balance a chemical equation: the method, three worked examples](https://freetoolhub.app/blog/balance-chemical-equations): A clear method for balancing chemical equations with three worked examples, plus the mistakes that make people lose marks and how to check your answer.
- [All guides](https://freetoolhub.app/blog)
